key_insight: Without an external quantum reference frame, a learner cannot assign different meanings to unseen quantum directions; if training states do not span the Hilbert space, all orthogonal unseen pure states collapse to the same prediction.
engineering_relevance: QML systems need explicit structure—such as feature maps, measurement bases, symmetry priors, locality assumptions, or diverse training states—because Hilbert-space dimension alone does not guarantee generalization.
method: Formulate supervised quantum learning without an external reference frame so predictions are basis-independent.
Prove that unspanned training data force equal predictions on all states orthogonal to the training span.
Extend the result to a robust setting under weak symmetry breaking and quantify the need for many oriented training directions.
evidence_signal: The paper combines theoretical proofs with numerical illustrations showing prediction collapse and its gradual relaxation under symmetry breaking.
watch_item: If the training set lacks sufficiently diverse, independently oriented quantum states, the model may appear expressive yet still fail to generalize to unseen directions.
paper_title: No Reference-Free Generalization in Quantum Machine Learning
